beats.text: Tomorrow's the vote. Tell me which ribbon you'll wear then; I'll happily lend you the other one today.

records.mechanism: A presses B to choose a supported person and adapts B's compromise until it reveals allegiance at the consequential moment.
records.confusableConcept: D55 seeks additional supporters for breadth; this scene centers on resolving B's divided loyalty between named alternatives.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Original B2 claims neutrality; revised A3 separates friendship from choice, and A5 tests B4's alternating ribbons against voting day.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b bargains sympathetically around friendship and timing; alternative a challenges the attribution of a substantive compromise.
records.reason: Original A5 returned to generic recruitment. Revised illustrative setting is a chess club election between friends. Internal second pass: fidelity 5 (A1/A3 demand a choice), logic 5 (B2 friendship informs A3; B4 rotation informs A5), relationship 4 (B protects friendships), heightening 4 (A5 isolates voting-day allegiance), specificity 4 (ribbons and timing), brevity/wit 4 (A will lend the rival ribbon when it matters less): 90. ABABA and word limit pass.
records.reservation: The ribbon is only a visible declaration, not proof of a private vote; the scene should keep its focus on expressed support.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 identifies obedience as the box's purpose; A5 adds a pointless return trip and forbids another question.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's purpose question becomes A3's compliance test; B4's completed delivery triggers A5's reversal.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks a reason, then B4 complies; A treats both the question and compliance as material for further testing.

heightening.evidence: A5 doubles the unnecessary movement and raises the behavioral requirement to unquestioning compliance.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an empty box, desk and direct workplace-style command.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 openly assigns the box an obedience-testing function; A5 makes its emptiness and return consequential.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring that empty box to my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What do you need it for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At present, to establish whether you'll bring it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Take it back without the question this time.

records.mechanism: A uses purposeless requests of increasing inconvenience to test whether B accepts A's authority without explanation.
records.confusableConcept: Delegate Downward assigns an unwanted responsibility through rank; here the otherwise pointless task exists to measure obedience.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A3 explicitly says the purpose is whether B will bring the box, and A5 immediately reverses the completed delivery.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a escalates after successful compliance by undoing the task; alternative b escalates after B reveals the physical discomfort of obeying.
records.reason: Retained unchanged: B4's completed delivery enables the unnecessary return and stricter compliance condition. Internal rereading confirms the original ratings.
records.reservation: The added inconvenience is modest in distance, though the wasted trip and prohibition on questions clearly increase the test.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 explicitly tests obedience without explanation, but A5's window closure may reduce inconvenience rather than increase it.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's question causes A3's explanation test; B4's cold causes A5's closure request, though 'remain instructional' is unclear.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks purpose and B4 reports discomfort, but A5 gives B no clear continuing physical task beyond closure.

heightening.evidence: A5 removes B4's source of discomfort and substitutes vague wording instead of a clearly greater inconvenience.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a window but no relationship or purpose; A5's 'remain instructional' is difficult to enact.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'remain instructional' strains for a phrase that does not specify what B should do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave your desk and stand by that open window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to know whether my team follows a direct request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's freezing. Can I get my coat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Fetch mine too, then come back and hold it while I check the rest of the team.

records.mechanism: A turns commands into tests of accepted authority and uses B's attempt to relieve discomfort to add another inconvenient obligation.
records.confusableConcept: An ordinary supervisor might request useful work; these commands primarily test compliance and accumulate unnecessary burden.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Original A3 names the explanation test; revised A3 names team obedience and A5 adds coat-holding while extending the wait.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b grants relief but attaches extra service and waiting; alternative a uses successful delivery as the occasion for a purposeless reversal.
records.reason: Original A5 eased the inconvenience and ended in unclear language. Revised office setting makes the supervisor relationship explicit. Internal second pass: fidelity 5 (A3 tests obedience; A5 adds burden), logic 5 (B2 causes stated test; B4's coat request causes added coat duty), relationship 4 (B negotiates warmth), heightening 4 (A5 adds service and waiting), specificity 4 (desk, window, coats), brevity/wit 4 (permission carries a new burden): 90. ABABA and word limit pass.
records.reservation: A's authority is deliberately petty; performance needs sincere assessment of compliance rather than pleasure in B's discomfort.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks the outgoing holder to tell everyone A is in charge; A3 rejects the key as sufficient public transfer.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's key-only offer causes A3's door/committee distinction; B4's assumed knowledge causes A5's request for audible relinquishment.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers the practical handoff and B4 sees announcement as redundant, resisting A's demand for explicit public transfer.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds the outgoing holder's publicly expressed cessation to A1's naming of the incoming authority.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a hall key and takeover; A3 identifies the committee as the audience.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's door understanding the key economically separates access from authority; A5 compresses the demand for relinquishment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the hall key and tell everyone I'm now in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The door will understand. The committee needs words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They know you're taking over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let them hear you stop.

records.mechanism: A demands that the current authority publicly identify A as the new decision-maker rather than merely hand over access.
records.confusableConcept: D57 seeks public standing or respect; D60 requires a transfer of decision authority from another person.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A1 explicitly pairs the key with naming A as in charge, and A5 asks B to make the relinquishment audible.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a moves from a physical key to public relinquishment; alternative b moves from occupying the chair to having authority announced to the room.
records.reason: Retained unchanged: the final demand develops B4's claim that succession is already understood. Internal rereading confirms the original ratings; preserving the dialogue also preserves the attributed public-statement seed.
records.reservation: A5's 'hear you stop' is compressed and less explicit than A1 about who decides next, but the full exchange supplies that meaning.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands being named as the decision-maker; A5 insists that B's acknowledgment reach the room.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's chair claim causes A3's location/succession distinction; B4's acknowledgment causes A5's audience correction.

relationship.evidence: B2 treats the occupied chair as sufficient and B4 concedes verbally, allowing A to pursue the remaining public requirement.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4's direct concession into a demand for public authorization before the meeting.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a departing meeting leader and A2 is absent; B2 supplies the occupied chair, with A5 naming the room.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 distinguishes furniture from succession; A5's 'I already agree' makes the audience problem concise and character-driven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before leaving the meeting, name me as the person who decides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're sitting in my chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Furniture announces location, not succession.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the room, please. I already agree.

records.mechanism: A requires the departing authority to name A publicly as the person empowered to decide.
records.confusableConcept: Occupying a prestigious seat or receiving a title can display status without transferring decision-making power.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A1 specifies 'the person who decides,' A3 distinguishes location from succession, and A5 requires the room to hear B's statement.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b accepts B's substantive concession and corrects its audience; alternative a additionally seeks an audible end to B's authority.
records.reason: Retained unchanged: B4 supplies the acknowledgment that A5 redirects to the necessary audience. Internal rereading confirms the original ratings and preserves the pair's attributed public-naming seed.
records.reservation: B4's volume is implicit in A5's correction; delivery must make the acknowledgment sound addressed to A rather than already announced.
